learn.title: Geometry on a grid
learn.body: Put points on the coordinate plane and geometry becomes arithmetic. Two questions come up all the time: how far apart are two points, and where is the point halfway between them?

learn.title: The distance formula
learn.body: For points $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$, the distance is $d=\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}$. It comes from a right triangle with the two points at the ends of the slanted side. We prove this in the next unit. On a horizontal or vertical line, just subtract.

learn.title: The midpoint formula
learn.body: The midpoint is the average of the coordinates: $M=\left(\frac{x_1+x_2}{2},\frac{y_1+y_2}{2}\right)$. It sits exactly halfway, so it is the same distance from both ends.

learn.title: Find an endpoint
learn.body: The midpoint of $AB$ is $M(3,4)$ and $A=(1,1)$. Find $B$.

questions.explanation: The points share a $y$-value, so subtract the $x$-values: $3-(-2)=5$.

questions.prompt: What is the $x$-coordinate of the midpoint of $(-4,2)$ and $(6,8)$?
The midpoint of $AB$ is $(2,1)$ and $A=(0,-3)$. What is $B$?
The distance formula is built from a \_\_ triangle.
questions.explanation: The horizontal and vertical changes are the two legs, and the distance is the slanted side.
